item.text: {"text":"Research supports distinguishing semantic similarity from functional relevance. Amazon’s [ESCI benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.06588) separates Exact, Substitute, Complement and Irrelevant query–product relationships, offering a useful diagnostic taxonomy. However, explicit search queries supply intent that interaction histories may lack; ESCI labels cannot be transferred directly to sequential recommendations. [EC4SRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.01347) also warns that sequence augmentation can create false positives and false negatives: a semantically close candidate is not automatically an unsuitable recommendation.\n\nSuggested adaptation, rather than an established benchmark: construct manually reviewed candidate pairs from available titles/descriptions, matching broad topic while varying one documented relation—explicit device compatibility, required accessory function, named artist or franchise. Record supporting text spans and distinguish direct connection, broad similarity, explicit contradiction and insufficient evidence. Shared artist identity establishes a connection, not user preference; missing compatibility documentation establishes uncertainty, not incompatibility. Abstain when ownership, required attributes or current intent are unknown. Measure pairwise ranking accuracy only on adjudicated pairs, alongside evidence coverage, abstention rate and reviewer agreement. Keep these auxiliary diagnostics separate from the fixed macro validation HR@10; use the literature’s taxonomy without importing datasets, pretrained weights or unavailable metadata."}
